Summary

SM120 (consumer Blackwell — RTX PRO 6000, DGX Spark) lacks the trtllm-gen precompiled cubins that SM100 uses for attention sinks. This adds an SM120-specific prefill path using flashinfer's fmha_v2 HMMA kernels, which support sinks natively via JIT compilation.

  • Add supports_fmha_v2_sm120_attention() in vllm/utils/flashinfer.py for SM120 detection
  • Extend can_use_trtllm_attention and use_trtllm_attention to include the SM120 fmha_v2 path
  • Update FlashInferBackend.supports_sink() to return True for SM120
  • Add SM120 fmha_v2 prefill dispatch using Q_PAGED_KV_NHD (reads directly from vLLM's paged KV cache, supports prefix caching and chunked prefill)
  • SM120 decode uses standard flashinfer (not trtllm-gen)
  • Skip FP8 Q quantization on SM120 (fmha_v2 doesn't support it)

Dependency

This PR requires the flashinfer kernel fix in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3106, which addresses a latent gate in determine_launch_params() that disabled flash_attention for Q_PAGED_KV layouts when max_kv_len < 16 — causing silent fallback to a non-flash-attention kernel that does not handle paged KV correctly.

Without that fix, short prompts or prefix-cached scenarios on SM120 produced non-deterministic, incorrect output. With it, attention is deterministic and correct.

Validation

I validated end-to-end on SM121a (DGX Spark GB10) with flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3106 applied:

  • Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct: deterministic batched prompts of lengths 2, 11, 22, 44 chars (all identical outputs for identical inputs)
  • Prefix caching enabled: warm + hit produces deterministic, coherent continuations
  • trl-internal-testing/tiny-GptOssForCausalLM (gpt_oss architecture with built-in attention sinks + sliding window + GQA): deterministic across repeated identical prompts
  • supports_sink() returns True on SM120
  • fmha_v2 HMMA kernels with sinks validated at kernel level (multiple configs: D=64/128, causal/non-causal, B=1-4, S=256-1024, sink values 0.01-10.0)
  • GQA (14 Q heads, 2 KV heads): produces coherent output matching triton_attn baseline within expected numerical precision

Known limitations

  • enforce_eager=True required (no CUDA graph support yet)
  • DECODER attention type only (no encoder/cross-attention)

AI assistance

AI assistance was used for investigation and code authoring. I reviewed every changed line, ran the validation above on real SM121a hardware, and verified the root-cause analysis of the upstream flashinfer bug.

Contributed by Second Nature Computing (https://joinsecondnature.com)

[Attention] Add SM120 fmha_v2 attention sink support for flashinfer b…
1f8a78a 
…ackend

SM120 (consumer Blackwell — RTX 5090, RTX PRO 6000, DGX Spark) lacks the
trtllm-gen precompiled cubins that SM100 uses for attention sinks. This
adds an SM120-specific prefill path using flashinfer's fmha_v2 HMMA
kernels, which support sinks natively via JIT compilation.

Changes:

- `vllm/utils/flashinfer.py`: add `supports_fmha_v2_sm120_attention()`
  helper. Extend `can_use_trtllm_attention` / `use_trtllm_attention` to
  recognize the SM120 fmha_v2 path. Add a `has_sliding_window` parameter
  that disqualifies the fmha_v2 path when any layer sets a sliding
  window — see below for why.

- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py`: `supports_sink()` now
  returns True for SM120. Add SM120 fmha_v2 prefill dispatch using
  `Q_PAGED_KV_NHD` so the kernel reads directly from vLLM's paged KV
  cache (correct under prefix caching and chunked prefill). The
  existing trtllm-gen path remains as the `else:` branch and inherits
  main's NVFP4 + canonicalize_singleton_dim_strides improvements
  preserved through the rebase. SM120 decode uses standard flashinfer
  (not trtllm-gen). Also threads `has_sliding_window=self.window_left != -1`
  through the metadata builder and asserts `self.window_left == -1`
  inside the fmha_v2 branch so any future regression fails loudly.

`trtllm_fmha_v2_prefill` expects `cum_seq_lens_kv` as cumulative TOKEN
lengths starting from 0. `TRTLLMPrefill` metadata stores PAGE indptrs in
that field (trtllm-gen uses them differently), so this builds the
proper token cumsum from `seq_lens`.

## Why the sliding-window disqualifier

The fmha_v2 SM120 path produces silently wrong output when a sliding
window is requested. The Python-side gate at
`flashinfer/prefill.py:4420` raises "Sliding window attention is not
yet supported for FMHAv2 on SM120 (Blackwell)" — but the underlying
fmha_v2 kernel tree implements sliding_window_causal masking and the
JIT codegen default generates those kernels for all SMs, so I first
investigated whether the gate was cosmetic.

Direct correctness test on SM121a (DGX Spark GB10), Q_PAGED_KV_NHD,
`seq_len ∈ {17, 33, 64, 128}`, `window_left ∈ {4, 8, 16, 32, 64}`,
with the Python gate monkey-patched out:

```
causal no-sliding:                 max_diff=0.0020  PASS
causal + sliding wl=8,  seq=64:    max_diff=2.02    FAIL
causal + sliding wl=16, seq=64:    max_diff=1.49    FAIL
causal + sliding wl=32, seq=64:    max_diff=1.26    FAIL
causal + sliding wl=16, seq=128:   max_diff=1.77    FAIL
causal + sliding wl=64, seq=128:   max_diff=0.94    FAIL
causal + sliding wl=4,  seq=33:    max_diff=2.36    FAIL
causal + sliding wl=8,  seq=17:    max_diff=1.64    FAIL
```

The SM120 codegen path really does not apply sliding window masking.
The Python gate is load-bearing, not cosmetic. The kernel fix belongs
upstream in flashinfer's SM120 fmha_v2 codegen and is out of scope.

In vLLM the fix is the `has_sliding_window` parameter described above,
which routes prefill through the standard flashinfer wrapper (which
does support sliding window) when any layer has `window_left != -1`.
Models with mixed sliding + full layers (e.g. gpt_oss) still hit the
existing `has_same_window_lefts` check in `FlashInferMetadataBuilder`,
independent of this change.

## Dependencies

Requires the following flashinfer PRs (open as of filing):
- flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3016 — sinks passthrough in
  `trtllm_fmha_v2_prefill`.
- flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3106 — latent gate in
  `determine_launch_params` that disabled `flash_attention` for
  `Q_PAGED_KV` when `max_kv_len < 16`, producing silently wrong output
  for short prompts.

## Validation on SM121a (DGX Spark GB10)

Validated post-rebase on 2026-05-27 against current main
(`origin/main` at `2d2c660104`). The rebased branch was checked out
in the editable vllm install; the test exercises the new SM120 fmha_v2
prefill path via FLASHINFER backend dispatch on actual hardware:

```
attention_backend = FLASHINFER       (confirmed in EngineCore log:
                                      "Using AttentionBackendEnum.FLASHINFER backend")
model             = trl-internal-testing/tiny-GptOssForCausalLM
                    (gpt_oss arch — has built-in attention sinks)
device            = NVIDIA GB10 (SM121a, compute capability 12.1)
dtype             = bfloat16
enforce_eager     = True

4 prompts × 16 tokens, temperature=0, seed=0:
  generation time: 0.88s
  determinism (rerun same seed): all 4 outputs match Run 1 byte-for-byte
  Result: PASS
```

Helper-level checks also verified on SM121a:
- `supports_fmha_v2_sm120_attention()` returns True
- `use_trtllm_attention(has_sliding_window=True)` returns False
  (sliding-window disqualifier wired correctly)
- `use_trtllm_attention(has_sliding_window=False)` returns True
- `FlashInferBackend` class imports cleanly against current main's
  `vllm.utils.torch_utils`

Output tokens from tiny-GptOssForCausalLM are not semantically
meaningful (the model is a ~100-param synthetic from trl-internal-testing
for testing purposes); the validation tests dispatch correctness and
determinism, not output quality. Full integration testing on production
sinks-using models (e.g. real gpt-oss-20b) is left to vLLM CI and
downstream deployment.

Rebased onto current main (2d2c660104) and squashed the original sliding-window disqualifier follow-up commit (b6372a1c70) into the main feature commit for a cleaner one-commit PR. This addresses the two mergify rebase notices (Apr 17, May 23). Not a new contribution — same PR, rebased.

Conflict resolution

Both touched files had churn from main since the PR base. Notable competing commits: 947138b6c2 (NVFP4 KV cache), 66dfee7121 (canonicalize_singleton_dim_strides for TMA stride canonicalization). Resolved by restructuring the prefill dispatch as if supports_fmha_v2_sm120_attention(): <SM120 fmha_v2 path> else: <main's evolved trtllm-gen path with NVFP4 + canonicalize improvements>. needs_fp8_out is initialized before the branch since main now references it post-block. The trtllm-gen call retains main's added sinks=self.sinks and kv_cache_sf=prefill_kv_block_scales parameters.

Earlier review feedback (gemini-code-assist, Apr 17)

The three high-priority items from the Apr 17 code review remain addressed in the rebased branch:

  • Docstring sliding-window correction → supports_fmha_v2_sm120_attention() docstring now states "Sliding window is NOT supported by fmha_v2 SM120 kernels today" with the kernel-side error message quoted.
  • torch.stack for K/V → no stack; the SM120 path uses Q_PAGED_KV_NHD layout to read directly from the paged KV cache.
  • Hardcoded bmm2_scale=1.0 → fmha_v2 prefill call uses bmm2_scale=self.bmm2_scale, which already accounts for _o_scale_float in __init__.

Validation on SM121a (DGX Spark GB10) post-rebase

  • attention_backend=FLASHINFER confirmed exercised (EngineCore log: "Using AttentionBackendEnum.FLASHINFER backend")
  • trl-internal-testing/tiny-GptOssForCausalLM, 4 prompts × 16 tokens, temperature=0, seed=0
  • Deterministic across two runs (all 4 outputs match Run 1 byte-for-byte)
  • Helper-level: supports_fmha_v2_sm120_attention() == True, use_trtllm_attention(has_sliding_window=True) == False on SM121a
  • pre-commit run --files vllm/utils/flashinfer.py vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py → all hooks pass (ruff, ruff format, typos, mypy, SPDX, lazy imports, forbidden imports, torch.cuda APIs, config docstrings, attention backend docs)

Full validation log in the squashed commit message. Tiny-GptOss output tokens aren't semantically meaningful (it's a ~100-param synthetic for path coverage); dispatch correctness and determinism are what's tested. Full real-model integration is left to vLLM CI and downstream deployment.

Per AGENTS.md: AI assistance was used (disclosed via the Co-Authored-By trailer in the commit). Ready for review.
